title: Chicken Enchilada Casserole
subtitle: Stacked tortillas, melted cheese
description: Stacked tortillas, melted cheese. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Brown seasoned beef
steps.instruction: Brown ground beef with taco seasoning and diced onion. Drain grease; stir in 1 cup enchilada sauce.

steps.title: Layer the casserole
steps.instruction: In a deep hotel pan: sauce, tortillas torn to fit, beef, cheese — repeat twice. Finish with sauce and cheese on top.

steps.title: Bake until bubbling
steps.instruction: Bake covered at 375°F 30 minutes; uncover and bake 15 more until cheese browns at edges.

steps.title: Rest and scoop
steps.instruction: Rest 10 minutes so layers set. Scoop Enchilada Casserole with a square spatula — it should hold its shape, not slide like soup.

proTips: Firefighters eat heavy after rough nights — double the protein if the hall had a busy shift.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Plate Chicken Enchilada Casserole with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Serve family-style from two full-size trays — never let the line run dry on a busy night.
Put starch and protein on separate trays so vegetarians can load up on sides.
Line up Chicken Enchilada Casserole on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Stacked tortillas, melted cheese. A hall pick for big-appetite nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
